200	We asked at the beginning of the class, we said, the first source is
201	that there is an angel called Laila who is in charge of pregnancy, and he determines, among other things, whether a person will be
202	foolish or wise.
203	After that we brought a second source, and we asked about the first: if a person is foolish or wise,
204	then a person who is foolish has a spirit of folly enter him, and one who has a spirit of folly enter him inevitably sins, and if
205	he sins then he is inevitably not a tzaddik, so if he is not...
206	If it is determined that he will be foolish already at birth, how can he be a tzaddik?
207	Because according to the first source, tzaddik and wicked are not determined, it is not said
208	to be determined at birth whether a person will be a tzaddik or wicked. So our first question: how can a person
209	be a tzaddik if it is determined that he will be foolish?
210	That is the question in general.
211	And the second question was: why do we need the tzaddikim in every single
212	generation at all?
213	Why are they planted in every single generation?
214	What is the benefit in that?
215	Up to here, do you have questions?
216	Comments?
217	And how is this connected to a true Rav?
218	How is this connected to a true Rav?
219	We also need to address that.
220	Who is a true Rav?
221	How do you choose a true Rav?
222	What is the benefit of a true Rav?
223	There are a great many questions about the subject of a Rav.
224	It is a very sensitive and very important subject.
225	So let's continue.
226	And to understand the matter, first we need to understand, we already introduced it, but now we will understand according to Rabash,
227	what is a wise person and what is a fool in spiritual work.
228	To understand the matter, we need to expand on and explain the words of our Sages, that the Holy One, Blessed Be He, decrees over the drop
229	whether it will be strong or weak, wise or foolish.
230	That is, one who is born weak, with no strength to overcome his inclination.
231	A weak person.
232	And born with a foolish desire.
233	That he is a fool.
234	And he has no talents.
235	And since also at the time of preparation, that is, when a person begins the work of HaShem, he must be
236	capable of receiving the Torah and wisdom.
237	As it is written, there is a verse that says, "He gives wisdom to the wise."
238	That is how it appears in the book of Daniel.
239	"He gives wisdom to the wise."
